title: How FOMO Cost Sir Isaac Newton a Fortune in the 1720 South Sea Bubble
alt_title_1: Why High IQ Fails Against Crowd Envy: Newton's 1720 Market Mistake
alt_title_2: Isaac Newton Cashed Out Early, Then Bought Back Near the 1720 Peak
description_hook: In 1720, Sir Isaac Newton booked roughly a 20,000-pound profit in South Sea Company shares, then watched friends grow rich, re-entered near summer highs above 900 pounds per share, and converted safe annuities into stock, losing 10,000 to 20,000 pounds.

scenes.headline: Newton Booked 20,000 Pounds, Then Chased the Top
scenes.stat_label: SIR ISAAC NEWTON IN THE SOUTH SEA BUBBLE
bullets: Cashed out early in spring 1720 for ~20,000-pound gain
Re-entered near summer peaks above 900 pounds per share
scenes.narration: In spring 1720, Sir Isaac Newton cashed out of South Sea Company stock early with roughly a twenty-thousand-pound profit, then lost a fortune chasing his friends back near the top.
scenes.source: Andrew Odlyzko, Notes and Records of the Royal Society (2018)

scenes.headline: Swapped Safe Annuities Near 900 Pounds a Share
scenes.stat_label: LOSS ON SWAPPED ANNUITIES AFTER AUTUMN CRASH
bullets: Watched wealthy peers multiply paper fortunes all summer
Lost 10,000 to 20,000 pounds when shares collapsed
scenes.narration: Archival research by historian Andrew Odlyzko shows Newton watched acquaintances get rich all summer, bought back near peaks above nine hundred pounds, and swapped safe annuities, finishing fifty-four percent worse off on those annuities.
scenes.source: Andrew Odlyzko, Notes and Records of the Royal Society (2018)

scenes.headline: Calculus Genius Cannot Outrun Social Comparison
scenes.left_body: Peers bragging at dinner -> abandons discipline -> buys mania peak
scenes.right_body: Accepts missed tail froth -> keeps realized 20,000-pound gain
scenes.narration: The physicist who invented calculus and mapped planetary motion still cracked under social comparison, proving that raw analytical IQ offers zero protection once watching neighbors get rich hijacks your discipline.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Odlyzko, Royal Society (2018)

scenes.headline: Enforce a 90-Day No-Chase Lockout After Selling
scenes.stat_label: WRITTEN RE-ENTRY RULES PRESERVE REALIZED GAINS
scenes.stat_subtext: Take profit -> park in T-bills -> 90-day ban on buying back higher
scenes.narration: Defend your portfolio with a written cool-down rule: whenever you sell an overheated asset at your target valuation, forbid yourself from buying that ticker back at a higher price for ninety days.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin protocol (advice, not a study)

scenes.headline: Temperament Protects What Intellect Builds
scenes.stat_label: NEVER LET A NEIGHBOR'S GAIN REWRITE YOUR PLAN
bullets: Missing the final 50% of a bubble costs zero real cash
Chasing back in at the top wipes out years of savings
scenes.narration: Market manias punish envy far harder than ignorance, so let written exit rules guard your capital when the crowd loses its head.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Odlyzko, Royal Society (2018)
